article_title: Quantum Science and Technologies in K-12: Supporting Teachers to Integrate Quantum in STEM Classrooms
citation: Holincheck, N.; Rosenberg, J.L.; Zhang, X.; Butler, T.N.; Colandene, M.; Dreyfus, B.W. (2024). Quantum Science and Technologies in K-12: Supporting Teachers to Integrate Quantum in STEM Classrooms. Educ. Sci. 14. https://www.mdpi.com/journal/education
title: National Q-12 Education Partnership discipline-specific frameworks structured around nine key quantum concepts
description: The National Q-12 Education Partnership released frameworks for integrating quantum concepts into specific K-12 disciplines: middle school STEM and high school computer science, physics, chemistry, and mathematics. They provide "guidance about how discipline-specific learning goals could be met through teaching quantum concepts" and are "all structured around nine key concepts", from quantum information science through quantum sensors. The article presents these frameworks as a resource to help teachers see where quantum fits within their existing disciplinary curricula.
requirements: Frameworks are intended for curriculum developers and teachers integrating quantum into discipline-specific K-12 learning goals.
constraints: The article notes few curricular resources are available for K-12 quantum education more broadly.
target_learners: K-12 students across elementary, middle, and high school
target_learning_goals: quantum science and technology concepts across STEM disciplines
examples: The article's workshop study asked teachers to connect quantum to their standards, with the Q-12 frameworks cited as support for understanding discipline-specific fit.
